  "text": "The station clock had stopped at twenty past four, though the trains continued to arrive late by other measures.

Mara found her brother beneath it, holding a cardboard box.

“You said a suitcase.”

“The zip went.”

She reached for the box, but he shifted it against his chest.

“It’s not heavy.”

In the car, he balanced it on his knees. Something inside clicked whenever she changed gear.

“Have you eaten?” she asked.

“On the train.”

She had bought bread, eggs, and the cereal he used to like. At the first traffic light, she wondered whether to mention the cereal.

Instead, she said, “The small room’s ready.”

“I won’t be long.”

“The window sticks. Don’t force it.”

At home, he put the box beside the bed and followed her into the kitchen. She filled the kettle while he stood near the table, still wearing his coat.

“You can hang that up.”

“Right.”

There were three hooks by the back door. He chose the one with a shopping bag on it, took the bag down, then hesitated.

“Anywhere,” she said.

While she made toast, he unpacked the box. Two mugs, a folded jumper, a bedside lamp. He brought one mug into the kitchen.

“This yours?” he asked.

She turned it over. A blue fish swam beneath a crack in the glaze.

“I wondered where that went.”

“I can wash it.”

She moved aside at the sink.

Later, carrying towels upstairs, she saw his coat on the hook. The shopping bag had been folded neatly beneath it.

His door was open. He was trying the lamp in the socket beside the bed.

“Does that work?” she asked.

He switched it on.

“Yes,” he said."
